subject: Arbiter Systems - Conditional bridging credit for GPU cost surge
messages:
From: Ravi Patel <ravi.patel@arbiter.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leah Gomez <leah.gomez@arbiter.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood reserved commit proposal - follow up

Ava — thanks for the deck and the proposal. Our CFO looked through the numbers and flagged the GPU exposure clause. If we lock a 36-month reserved commitment we need protection in case spot GPU pricing doubles — otherwise the economics break for our product roadmap.

Two asks from our side: 1) a short-term bridging credit if market GPU unit costs spike >25% vs. baseline for any rolling 90-day window, and 2) a passback/true-up mechanism tied to a public GPU index (we suggested the global-gpu-index link in the spreadsheet).

Can Redwood provide an example of how the bridging credit would flow and what approvals are required internally? We'd like to avoid legal redlines but need something that mitigates material risk.

—Ravi
Head of Platform Ops
Arbiter Systems
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Ravi Patel <ravi.patel@arbiter.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood reserved commit proposal - follow up

Ravi — appreciate the straight questions. Short answer: yes, we can structure a limited bridging credit and a GPU-indexed true-up, but it requires finance sign-off on exposure limits and an exec-level discount carve-out for index-triggered credits.

Attached: a worked example (gpu_index_passback_model.xlsx) and a draft operational MOP clause (mop_bridge_draft.docx) showing the mechanics. High level: if the agreed baseline GPU benchmark increases by >25% for a rolling 90-day window, Redwood will apply a capped bridging credit equal to 30% of the incremental per-token cost above baseline for up to 60 days. The credit is applied as an account-level invoice credit and can be netted against monthly usage. After 60 days we move to a scheduled true-up which either adjusts unit pricing prospectively or triggers a negotiated rebate.

Kimberly & Marcus — can you review exposure and provide the maximum credit cap we'd be comfortable authorizing for a deal of Arbiter's size (deal_id ARB-2026-1124)? David, please flag any operational constraints for applying short-term invoice credits at account level.

Next steps suggested: finance provides cap suggestion by EOD tomorrow, then I'll loop in Legal for tidy contract language.

Thanks — Ava
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Arbiter bridging credit - exposure calc

Team — ran the model with Arbiter's proposed commit (36 months, 1.2M reserved GPU-hours annually). Key outputs in gpu_index_passback_model.xlsx:
- Baseline unit cost (internal): $0.022/token-equivalent GPU unit
- 25% uplift breach -> incremental cost exposure ~ $220k/month at Arbiter's expected throughput
- Proposed 30% bridging credit reduces immediate exposure to ~$154k/month for the 60-day window

Recommendation: cap aggregate bridging credit for this deal at $225k per occurrence (90-day rolling triggers count separately, but cap applies per-trigger event per rolling year). Rationale: keeps executive cost exposure bounded while offering meaningful protection to the customer.

If Legal accepts the MOP wording, this cap should be acceptable for Commercial approval. Any change to the cap requires Director-level approval.

Marcus
Head of Revenue Finance
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 08:19:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Arbiter bridging credit - legal and ops notes

Ava/Marcus — legal has a couple of clean-up asks on the MOP clause (we prefer defined index source and a single remediation path — either credit OR price adjustment, not both automatically). Also: operations flagged one implementation detail — we need an internal journal code to apply these credits so billing and usage reporting remain reconciled.

David: can ops create the journal code and confirm ETA? If we can apply credits within two billing cycles (60 days) we can accept the prospective cap Marcus suggested.

Ravi: from a commercial standpoint we can accept the proposed structure if Arbiter is comfortable with the per-trigger cap and the fixed 60-day bridging window followed by a negotiated true-up. Would you prefer invoice credit or prospective rate adjustment as the primary remediation?

—Kimberly
Director, Strategic Accounts
From: Ravi Patel <ravi.patel@arbiter.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leah Gomez <leah.gomez@arbiter.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 16:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Arbiter bridging credit - legal and ops notes

Kimberly — thanks for the clarity and quick turnaround. Arbiter's preference is invoice credit for the 60-day bridging window (keeps our month-to-month cashflow predictable). We accept the $225k per-trigger cap and the single-remediation model (credit then negotiated adjustment).

Please proceed to finalize MOP wording and I'll route to our procurement for signature once we have DocuSign-ready language. Attaching a short note with our internal procurement approver details (procurement@arbiter.ai).

Looking forward to the final draft.

Best,
Ravi
